business_scope.primary_industry_name: Endowment Management for Philanthropic and Scientific Grants

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law, Local Statutes, and Customary Land Law)

Samoa–People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty for the Promotion and Protection of Investments

Agreement between Samoa and Australia for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (2010)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1988, as amended by the International Companies Amendment Act 2009 (beneficial ownership register requirements) and the International Companies Amendment Act 2011; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007 (No. 20 of 2007), as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) directives issued pursuant to the said Act; Companies (Fees) Regulations made under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; and the Incorporated Foundations (if any) recognized under Samoa legal practice, subject to the Registrar of International Companies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the natural person founder's valid passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority in the country of origin plus a licensed Samoa Notary Public or Commissioner for Oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Competent Authority in the country of origin (Samoa is party to the Hague Apostille Convention); for non-Apostille countries, Consular Legalization via the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or nearest Samoan diplomatic/consular mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incumbency and director/shareholder resolution of the corporate founder (where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or company registry of the founder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as required by Samoa AML/CFT regulations

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML source-of-wealth and bank reference letter from a regulated financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Overseas bank or licensed financial institution maintaining the founder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille/Consular Legalization if requested by the Samoa registered agent or FIU

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO declaration and organizational structure chart (ultimate beneficial ownership piercing schedule)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate service provider or licensed Samoa registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal due diligence verification; requires legalization only for jurisdictions outside the Apostille network

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence in accordance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007; mandatory screening of all founders, directors, shareholders, and beneficiaries against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) alert lists, United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, United States OFAC SDN List, and Her Majesty's Treasury/OFC consolidated sanctions list; enhanced due diligence mandatory where any person identified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), family member, or close associate; negative screening results to be documented and retained for a minimum of five years from termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry (Registrar of International Companies), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa — filings effected through licensed Samoa registered agents and the MCIL E-Registries filing channel
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory filing language is English; names may be selected in a foreign script but must be transliterated into the Latin (English) alphabet; the registered name must be capable of being rendered in English characters for the Samoa register; every International Company must maintain a name that is distinguishable from existing registered names and must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc', or an approved equivalent suffix when required by the International Companies Act 1988.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Foundation (where implying a regulated charitable trust operator without prior licensing)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its licensed registered agent may file a written application for reconsideration with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds of objection and attaching supporting evidence; if the Registrar maintains the refusal, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 21 calendar days of the reconsideration decision, with a copy to the Attorney General's Chambers; the Minister's determination is subject to judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa by way of an application for prerogative writ.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for an International Company or Charitable Endowment Foundation; a physical registered office in Samoa is mandatory at all times, maintained by a licensed registered agent; purely administrative back-office functions may be virtualized, but the statutory registered office and custody of statutory records must be physically located in Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Risk_Standard — quantified risk estimated at 10–20% within the first twelve months; the International Companies Registry and the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour may conduct or commission document-based substance verification, and unannounced physical inspections may occur where economic substance filings or beneficial ownership records are deficient, in accordance with the International Companies Amendment Act 2011 and anti-money laundering supervision protocols.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office services (year one, including AML/CFT compliance oversight)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for licensed trust and corporate services providers in Apia

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, authentication, and Hague Apostille/Consular Legalization of founder documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP/sanctions screening, and AML/CFT onboarding compliance bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider / retained compliance counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for international corporate due diligence opinions in Samoa

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 4-9 (incorporation), s. 12 (registered office and registered agent), s. 15 (objects and powers), s. 29 (directors); International Companies (Fees) Regulations; International Companies (Amendment) Act 2011; general savings provisions of the Companies Act 2001 (Samoa) where not inconsistent.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa; supervisory authority vesting in the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for international companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Certificate of Incorporation under Form IC-1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association submitted under Section 4 of the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no mandatory escrow account. The international company may issue one or more shares of any nominal value stated in its articles. Charitable endowment assets must be held separately and recorded in the books of the Samoa international company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscriber to the Memorandum of Association subscribes to one ordinary share at par value US$1.00, and the President is authorized to issue a share certificate on payment. (2) The registered office at [Address], Apia, Samoa is adopted as the company’s registered office. (3) [Name], [Name] and [Name] are appointed President, Secretary and Treasurer respectively, each to serve until removed by the board. (4) The appointed officers are jointly authorized to open bank accounts, execute grant agreements, incur ordinary administrative expenses, and file all statutory notices. (5) This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, MCIL, Apia, Samoa through a licensed SIFA registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed company names in English to the Registrar through a licensed registered agent. The Registrar reserves an approved name for 30 days. The agent conducts availability screening and arranges preliminary review of the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Passport copy of subscriber or shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused under Section 7(3) of the International Companies Act 1987, the applicant may re-submit a different name within 10 business days through the same registered agent without incurring an additional name reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, consent of the registered agent, and payment of the government registration fee. The Registrar examines the documents and, upon compliance, issues the Certificate of Incorporation with a unique registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of registered office and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query, the registered agent may file corrective schedules within 14 business days. Clerical or formal deficiencies do not require re-payment of the registration fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Registered Agent Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Samoa-licensed international company management provider to serve as registered office and registered agent. File the notice of appointment and registered office address with the Registrar within 30 days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form IC-3 Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected, file an amended Form IC-3 through the agent. If a registered agent resigns, the company has 30 days under Section 12(4) of the Act to appoint a replacement or face potential registry action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution in accordance with the Articles. Adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and appointment of President, Secretary, and Treasurer. Keep the executed minutes and register of officers at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting or written consent resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A procedural defect in the board resolution may be cured by convening a fresh board meeting and ratifying all prior actions under Section 45 of the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Charitable Foundation Authorization and Operating Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Charitable Organization Unit, in coordination with Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for formal recognition as a charitable endowment entity by submitting the constitutional charitable purposes, grant-making policies, and internal financial controls. Obtain the Charitable Endowment Operation Permit before making any donor-funded grant distributions.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association setting out exclusively charitable or scientific purposes
Grant-making policy and financial control manual
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, amend the constitutional purposes or financial control documents and re-submit within 30 days. A refusal may be appealed to the Chief Executive Officer of MCIL within 20 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Identification and Exemption Status Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Government of Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a Samoa taxpayer identification number (TIN) and apply for recognition of the charitable tax-exempt status under the Income Tax Act 2012. Confirm that the international company conducted no domestic revenue-generating activity and is entitled to tax-exempt zone treatment.
required_dossiers: Statement of non-resident ownership and proposed activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An adverse tax classification may be appealed to the Ministry for Revenue within 20 working days, supported by the constitutional charitable-purpose clause and the absence of commercial trading in Samoa.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Charitable Organization Unit, with oversight by Samoa International Finance Authority for international companies
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Charitable Endowment Operation Permit and Certificate of Charitable Organization Registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Environment Protection Agency (SEPA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 - Exempt / Administrative Registration only (office-based endowment management and grant administration; no physical manufacturing, construction, or industrial installation)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered at formation stage; the activity involves no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation. If the foundation later funds or operates a laboratory, clinic, or physical facility, a full environmental impact assessment under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 (Samoa) and SEPA discharge, waste, and emissions standards will be required prior to commencement of physical operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority; building occupancy clearance from the Apia District Town and Village Planning Authority; and workplace safety compliance under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 (Samoa), including employee registration with the Samoa Accident Compensation Corporation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MaF), Independent State of Samoa; e-filing portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Incorporate the International Company (IC) with the Registrar of International Companies (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour) under the International Companies Act 1987. A tax-exempt IC does not require a TIN or VAGST ID. Where a TIN is required for banking, licensing, or grant account purposes, file MfR Form TIN-01 together with the Certificate of Incorporation, registered office certificate, trust deed or charter, and passport copies of directors and beneficiaries; issuance typically takes 3-5 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist in Samoa. Automatic tax exemption applies by operation of Section 192 of the International Companies Act 1987, exempting the IC from income tax, VAGST, stamp duty, and exchange control. For any incidental onshore charitable activity conducted outside the IC structure, an Income Tax Exemption Certificate for charitable organizations may be obtained from the MfR under the Income Tax Ordinance 1959 (as amended).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the VAGST Act 2007
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual value of taxable supplies; mandatory registration once the 12-month rolling turnover exceeds this threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing approval, or digital stamping mandate is currently enforced. VAGST returns must be filed electronically via the MaF e-filing portal; invoices must disclose the supplier TIN, VAGST registration ID, and separately stated tax amount.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services supplied to non-residents—including offshore endowment management, grant administration, and philanthropic treasury and investment services to foreign beneficiaries—are zero-rated under the VAGST Act 2007. A tax-exempt IC is entirely outside the VAGST net; if the IC voluntarily registers for VAGST, full zero-rating attaches to export supplies supported by evidence of offshore consumption and settlement in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs, Ministry for Revenue)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a licensed commercial bank in Samoa
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: MfR audit powers extend six years over zero-rating claims. Improper claims are reassessed at 15% VAGST, attract a shortfall penalty of up to 100% of the underpaid tax, and default interest at 20% per annum; fraudulent evasion is prosecuted under the Tax Administration Act 2015, with retrospective clawback, fines, and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), acting under the Exchange Control Act 1977, the Exchange Control Regulations 1977 and the Financial Institutions Act 1996; the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) supervises the International Company register and offshore compliance interface.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates a managed float for the Samoan Tala (WST), with the Central Bank of Samoa administering all dealings in foreign exchange through licensed authorised dealers (commercial banks). Current-account convertibility (grants, donations, fees, trade settlements) is broadly available, whereas capital-account transactions (investment flows, portfolio transfers, external borrowings) require case-by-case CBS approval. The WST is not quoted on any international electronic trading venue and is practically non-convertible offshore, so cross-border endowment flows must be settled in USD, AUD, EUR or NZD. The International Company (IC) is classified as a non-resident for exchange-control purposes: foreign-currency endowment receipts, donation inflows and grant outflows may be routed through a CBS-approved external account without forced conversion into WST, and remittances of foundation funds to foreign grantees are not subject to profit-remittance withholding, tax clearance or CBS surrender obligations. The only genuine remittance hurdle is evidentiary: the CBS and reporting banks require the underlying endowment deed, donor source-of-funds documentation and foundation grant policy to be produced whenever a wire is questioned.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1977, a resident exporter must receive the export proceeds within three months from the date of shipment and must offer 100% of the foreign currency proceeds to an authorised dealer for conversion into WST within one month of receipt; extensions are granted by the CBS only on written application. This statutory surrender timeline and full (100:100) conversion ratio apply to resident operational receipts but do not govern the IC charitable endowment: the foundation is a non-resident external entity holding an external account, and its donation and grant flows are exempt from the surrender obligation. Should the IC ever receive WST-denominated income inside Samoa through a resident account, the one-month surrender duty and 100% conversion ratio would apply to that receipt.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: External Operational Account in USD/AUD/WST (endowment escrow and grant disbursement)
External Operational Account in WST/USD with domestic grant-paying capability
External Operational Account in WST/USD; capital escrow holding account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BSP Samoa Limited (Westpac Samoa banking business successor)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: External Operational Account in USD/AUD with Pacific-region correspondent reach

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW. Samoa maintains no digital-bank or electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing category, and the CBS does not authorise non-bank cross-border money transmission in WST. Offshore digital EMIs (multi-currency neobanks and payment platforms) are not recognised as exchange-control authorised dealers in Samoa, cannot hold a CBS-designated external account on behalf of the IC, and are commonly rejected by correspondent banks when the underlying beneficiary is a Samoan offshore entity. The only defensible use is auxiliary: an offshore EMI may collect small donor contributions in USD/EUR at the IC's instruction with immediate same-day settlement onward to the CBS-licensed external account; however, such EMIs must never become the primary treasury or grant-disbursement rail because of sanctions-screening gaps, lack of SIFA-compliant recordkeeping and elevated de-risking risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for first-time onboarding of a non-resident International Company. At least one director who is also a natural-person beneficial owner (or the licensed Samoan registered agent accompanied by the authorised signatory) must attend an in-person KYC interview at the commercial bank in Apia; fully remote or video-only opening is not generally available to ICs at Bank of Samoa, SCB or BSP, and ANZ Samoa will consider a concierge hybrid interview only where the remaining directors are verified through apostilled notarial certificates and a power of attorney in favour of a Samoan resident signatory. The interview must be supported by original or certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency, good-standing certificate, beneficial-owner register, board resolution appointing signatories and the SIFA registered-agent acknowledgement; all signatories must execute specimen signature cards in the presence of a bank officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholding under the International Companies Act 1987 conceals ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA Certificate of Good Standing and Certificate of Incumbency; complete UBO register with full legal name, nationality, date of birth and residential address of each natural-person controller; signed nominee declaration disclosing 100% underlying ownership; certified passports and utility-bill proof of address of every BO; independent sanctions and PEP screening report for each BO conducted by the bank or a licensed international service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Charitable endowment purpose appears broad, unverifiable or inconsistent with ISIC 6430 treasury activities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the IC charter and Articles stating the philanthropic and scientific grant-making object; foundation board resolution adopting an endowment management and grant-disbursement policy; SIFA acceptance of the registered charitable scope; Ministry of Revenue tax-exempt status letter; a written grant-making policy covering thematic areas, selection criteria, geographic scope, maximum grant size and disbursement calendar.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial donor endowment source-of-funds cannot be established (charitable facade money-laundering typology)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full donor KYC pack: for natural-person donors, certified passport and bank reference; for institutional donors or corporates, board resolution resolving the donation and audited financial statements evidencing lawful surplus; source-of-wealth narrative and prior bank statements; executed endowment and donation agreement containing claw-back and anti-money-laundering warranties; donor name and jurisdiction screened against sanctions and adverse media.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Grant distribution to foreign beneficiaries may be diverted to terrorist financing or sanctions circumvention
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recipient due-diligence file containing certificate of registration or charitable status of every grantee; verified identity of the beneficiary institution's authorised officer; sanctions and terrorism-list screening under Samoa FIU, UN, OFAC and EU directives; signed grant agreement with restricted-use covenants, annual acquittal and re-grant prohibition; bank-approved SWIFT standing settlement instructions pre-verified for each grantee to prevent payment redirection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: External-account classification and single-tranche inbound endowment wire triggers CBS exchange-control scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBS external-account approval letter naming the IC; board resolution specifically authorising the donation and identifying the bank; executed foundation deed and donor agreement; remittance advice with coded beneficiary reference (SIFA number plus 'Charitable Endowment'); a statutory declaration of source of funds for any wire at or above the bank's enhanced due-diligence threshold; an itemised grant pipeline and cash-flow projection demonstrating genuine charitable deployment of the liquidity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered agent appears as a shell arranger and the foundation lacks effective substance in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Agreement with a SIFA-licensed registered agent and confirmation of physical office, custody of statutory records and minutes in Samoa; appointment of a Samoan resident licensed auditor; evidence of periodic board meetings convened through the registered office in Apia; CBS-compliant accounting ledgers maintained in Samoa; registered-agent attestation to the economic purpose of the foundation and its grant programme.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Endowment contributions and donor grants must be injected by SWIFT MT103 to the IC's CBS-approved external account at a licensed commercial bank, with SWIFT field 59 carrying the IC's exact legal name and SIFA registration number and field 70 narrative reading 'Donation - Charitable Endowment / ISIC 6430'; the remitting donor bank must use its true originator details to avoid correspondent rejection. The receiving Samoan bank verifies the CBS external-account authorisation, and wires at or above the bank's enhanced due-diligence threshold require the executed endowment deed, donor KYC pack and board resolution before the credit is released. Inward WST-denominated donations are accepted and credited to the external account at the managed-float rate with CBS reporting, while USD/AUD/EUR donations are retained in kind; no NDF or prepaid-instrument structuring is required because the IC is exchange-control non-resident. The IC should pre-agree with the bank an inbound-wire checklist covering donor name, donor country, purpose code, underlying instrument, expected date and amount so that large endowment injections do not fail at correspondent-bank screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Grant outflows clear via SWIFT MT103 beneficiary transfers (with MT202 cover where split value-dating is used) through the bank's correspondent network, typically ANZ Australia/New Zealand, BSP Fiji/PNG or a US clearing bank, directly to grantee accounts or to research and scientific suppliers under grant-funded procurement. Because the IC is non-resident, external-account-to-external-account grant payments need no prior CBS exchange-control approval; only conversions into WST for local charitable operations require an authorised-dealer spot transaction and CBS notification. Commercial Letters of Credit are a legitimate secondary rail where endowment funds procure scientific equipment or laboratory consumables: the domestic bank may issue an irrevocable LC against the endowment's USD collateral held in a segregated escrowed account, with CBS approval of the underlying import. For repeat grantees, pre-approved SSI records and a disbursement calendar attached to the foundation's grant policy reduce friction; zero-value test wires and same-day reversal patterns must be avoided as they are recognised layering red flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/WST forward contracts with a CBS-licensed authorised dealer where the IC has a scheduled WST-denominated disbursement in Samoa, tenor generally capped at 12 months and approved on a case-by-case basis by the Central Bank.

Cross-currency swaps (USD against AUD, EUR or NZD) with the depository bank or a permitted overseas counterparty, used solely to match multi-currency endowment liabilities and subject to CBS notification and bank credit approval.

Offshore over-the-counter non-deliverable forwards on the Samoan Tala (WST NDF), technically available to non-resident holders of external accounts but practically dormant because no continuous WST NDF benchmark exists; use is not recommended except in rare two-way quotes from large Australasian banks.

Natural hedging through a multi-currency external-account ladder (USD/AUD/EUR/NZD) with maturity-matched grant liabilities, requiring zero regulatory approval and operating as the IC's default zero-derivative treasury policy for a charitable endowment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Compliance Declaration (Form IC-AR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) – Registry of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than 90 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 50 per month; a second reminder triggers suspension of corporate functions; failure for 90 days leads to administrative strike-off and vesting of assets in the Public Trustee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registration Fee Payment under the International Companies Act 1987
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A civil penalty equal to 10% of the unpaid fee accrues immediately; continued non-payment for 90 days is cause for certificate revocation and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following each tax year end (30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew triggers retroactive revocation of charitable tax exemption, a late-filing penalty of 20% on exempt net income, and potential denial of grant-maker recognition.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory independent audit is compulsory only if: (a) total charitable assets managed exceed WST 300,000 (approx. USD 16,000); (b) annual gross grant distributions exceed WST 800,000 (approx. USD 42,000); or (c) the foundation is licensed by SIFA as a public charitable institution. Otherwise, the foundation may file unaudited internal accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Samoa, with IFRS for SMEs permitted for entities not engaged in public interest activities. Financial statements must be prepared in English or Samoan and presented showing income, expenses, and grant disbursements separately.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent maintains the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership on behalf of the foundation. Separate annual UBO filing is not required; instead, each share transfer or beneficial ownership change must be notified to the registered agent in writing within 14 days, and the annual return must be accompanied by a beneficial ownership confirmation certificate.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for the exempt International Company (IC); Samoa's general resident corporate income tax rate is 27% under the Income Tax Act 2015
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 100% statutory exemption from corporate income tax, dividend withholding tax, capital gains tax and stamp duty for licensed ICs under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), Part XII exemption; the only recurring Government impost is the annual license fee (US$150-US$1,000 per authorized share capital tier); charitable endowment income is outside the Samoan source taxation rule

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Annual Return & Government Fee Statement (Form ICA-AR-1); filed electronically through the Samoa International Companies Registry portal administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), exclusively by the licensed Samoan registered agent on behalf of the non-resident entity
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Government license fee is due on each incorporation anniversary; the Annual Return must be submitted within 30 days after the anniversary date (International Companies Act 1987, s.113)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the IC and its unique registry number as shown on the certificate of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the registry record exactly; non-resident directors provide the certificate details to the Samoan agent who pre-fills the form

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical street address of the licensed registered agent in Apia where statutory records are maintained
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No PO Box permitted; the non-resident principal designates the agent, who confirms the office address and statutory inspection hours

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full name, residential address, nationality and date of birth of each director
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confidential and not publicly searchable; non-resident directors require no Samoan residence, work permit or Government approval

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address and shareholding of each member of the entity operated as a private charitable foundation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited; the register is kept at the registered office and is disclosed only to authorized regulators and the agent for AML purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 5 - Authorized and Issued Share Capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital by class, par value and number of shares issued; determines the Government fee tier
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Denominated in USD or WST; the agent computes the fee tier from the declared authorized capital stated in the constitutional documents

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attestation by the Samoan offshore services provider that customer due diligence, beneficial ownership records and the registered office are in place
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must hold a current offshore services provider license and is the primary compliance interface for non-resident principals

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the IC has not carried on business in Samoa and has derived no Samoan-source income during the reporting year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Critical for preserving the 0% tax status; a false declaration attracts fraud penalties, retrospective taxation and deregistration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tiered fee calculation based on authorized share capital (US$150 / US$500 / US$1,000) payable to the Samoan Treasury
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Paid by wire transfer through the registered agent; the Treasury receipt number is endorsed on the e-filing before submission

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic signature of a director or the registered agent certifying the accuracy and completeness of the return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compliant electronic authorization suffices; the original signed copy is retained in the agent's AML file and need not be mailed to Samoa

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Annual Return incurs a fixed penalty of approximately WST 200 per return; unpaid annual Government fees accrue monthly surcharges until settled; continued default beyond six months triggers strike-off and deregistration, with reinstatement conditioned on payment of all arrears, the statutory restoration fee and fresh agent certification

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends and capital distributions made by the exempt International Company; the statutory non-resident dividend withholding rate of 15% under the Income Tax Act 2015 applies only to resident companies outside the IC regime
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the IC is statutorily exempt, no Samoan withholding tax arises on outbound grants, dividends or repatriations; where any residual Samoan-source payment is nonetheless characterized as taxable, the non-resident recipient must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its own tax authority, (ii) lodge the TRC together with a beneficial ownership self-declaration to the Samoan withholding agent and the Ministry for Revenue before payment, and (iii) obtain written certification of the reduced DTA rate prior to remittance; treaty relief is denied retroactively if the documentation is not supplied within the statutory filing window
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% for the exempt IC in respect of IP royalties and debt interest paid by the foundation; for resident Samoan payers the statutory non-resident withholding rate is 15% on royalties and 15% on interest; under applicable Samoa double tax agreements (e.g., the Samoa-New Zealand DTA) interest and royalty rates are commonly reduced to 10%, subject to presentation of a valid Tax Residency Certificate and satisfaction of the beneficial ownership test

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Samoa-specific Local File or Master File thresholds; the Income Tax Act 2015 applies the arm's length principle to cross-border dealings of resident taxpayers, but the exempt IC is outside the TP documentation regime and no local-currency filing threshold is triggered for the tax-exempt endowment entity
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa has not enacted Economic Substance Regulations in the BVI/Cayman sense. However, the IC regime statutorily requires each company to maintain a licensed registered agent, a physical registered office in Samoa, complete books and records, and an annual return; this imposed presence is the substance baseline that prevents recharacterization as a shell or as a Samoan tax resident. Endowment management must be documented with board minutes, investment records and grant approval papers to satisfy OECD/EU substance reviews and bank counterparty due diligence

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely declaring the 'no Samoan business' exemption while managing Samoan assets, deriving Samoan-source income, or soliciting contributions from the Samoan public; deliberately omitting material facts in filings to the Ministry for Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax shortfall penalty up to 150% of the underpaid tax, plus statutory interest and criminal fines up to WST 100,000; imprisonment for up to 7 years for fraudulent tax declarations; cancellation of the IC's exempt status and deregistration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the registered agent are jointly and severally liable for restitution of unpaid taxes and penalties; the Samoan courts may freeze personal bank accounts, issue warrants of arrest and impose departure bans pending resolution of the tax debt

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a passive nominee address with no director oversight, no accounting records, no board minutes and no genuine grant-making activity; paying the annual fee solely to maintain a letterbox without the required economic footprint
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off and deregistration under the International Companies Act; penalties for failure to keep records; disqualification of the registered agent; reinstatement granted only upon payment of arrears and restoration fees and production of substantiated records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for reinstatement costs and third-party losses caused by the sham; court-ordered disqualification from acting as a director for up to 5 years; personal liability for false annual return declarations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing endowment contributions or grant distributions without customer due diligence, beneficial ownership verification or suspicious transaction reports; conducting unlicensed financial activity disguised as charitable grants; evading FIU reporting obligations under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines up to WST 1,000,000; revocation of the international company license and the agent license; confiscation of the funds involved; adverse regulatory findings that cause reciprocal blacklisting of the agent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual fines up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 14 years for money laundering offences; travel bans and asset restraint orders pending trial; directors personally responsible for AML compliance failures within the foundation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a 'private charitable foundation' and soliciting donations or distributing grants without the required statutory registration/license (Charitable Trusts Act 1965 and the regulatory license condition attached to ISIC 6430 endowment activity); misappropriating funds earmarked for philanthropic or scientific purposes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cease-and-desist orders; fines up to WST 25,000 for unregistered charitable solicitation; court-ordered restitution and freezing of the foundation's bank accounts; retrospective cancellation of the tax exemption with reassessment on all managed assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for equitable restitution of misapplied grant monies; disqualification from managing charities; criminal prosecution for theft and fraudulent conversion carrying custodial sentences; personal travel bans imposed on evidence of dissipation of foundation assets
